entries.title: XDNA2 IRON design and compile-only contract
entries.tags: iron program runtime worker objectfifo acquire release fill drain npu2 aie2p compile xclbin insts
entries.body: Emit design.py --dev npu2 --emit-mlir once, with kernel.cc as the only external source. The trusted repository driver parses the saved device, compiles the same source with Peano, and inspects linked core symbols and xclbin/instruction artifacts. Offline validation supports explicit tiles, finite workers, acquire/release windows and static DMA tasks. Host execution uses the exact C++ body with approved headers; unknown intrinsics and MLIR operations are unsupported. Compilation alone is not numerical validation or NPU binary execution.

entries.title: XDNA2 elementwise streaming and Peano kernel rules
entries.tags: add gamma moving average elementwise peano externalfunction vector tile alignment objectfifo
entries.body: Use one or more fixed-size ObjectFifo tiles between shim, memory, and compute endpoints. The Worker must acquire all inputs and the output, call an ExternalFunction whose arg_types exactly match the Peano extern C signature, then release every acquired element. Choose tile sizes that divide the static tensor extent and respect vector alignment. Start with scalar C++ loops when vector API legality is uncertain; optimize only after that root compiles. For elementwise binary operations, a single Worker and two input FIFOs plus one output FIFO is the reliable baseline. Do not pass scalar values with an ABI that differs from ExternalFunction arg_types.

entries.title: XDNA2 reduction design
entries.tags: reduce reduction sum max min accumulation whole input output one element
entries.body: The official vector-reduce pattern sends the whole fixed input to one compute tile, invokes one reduction kernel, and drains a one-element output. A reduction tile cannot be treated as independent elementwise output tiles unless partial sums are explicitly combined. Preserve the declared accumulation dtype and reduction order requirements. A safe root uses one Worker and a scalar or known-good vectorized Peano reduction; multi-core partial reductions are optimization proposals only when the final combine is represented and compiled.

entries.title: XDNA2 matrix multiplication tiling and precision
entries.tags: matmul gemm tile m n k cascade float16 float32 accumulation whole array
entries.body: Tile M, N, and K so every local buffer has a fully static type and all FIFO transfers agree with the Peano kernel ABI. FP16 or bfloat16 inputs should accumulate in float32 when the semantic IR requires it. K tiling changes floating-point association and may introduce extra truncations if partial results are stored at lower precision. Begin with the official single-core structure; whole-array and cascade designs are later proposals. A cascade proposal must distribute K partial products and combine every contribution before draining output.

entries.title: XDNA2 transpose data movement constraints
entries.tags: transpose dma stride vshuffle tensor access pattern int32 float32 layout
entries.body: A transpose may be expressed through DMA access patterns or a compute kernel. Shim DMA stride-one accesses must be at least four bytes, so the pure-DMA strategy is appropriate for 32-bit values but not smaller element widths. For general shapes, use static TensorAccessPattern dimensions and verify divisibility. Hybrid layouts use DMA for outer tiles and VSHUFFLE for inner blocks; do not reuse a specialized shuffle kernel for an unsupported dtype or block size. FP32 has four-byte elements and can use the same byte-level DMA legality as int32 while preserving its element type.

entries.title: XDNA2 softmax and nonlinear kernels
entries.tags: softmax exp max reduce sum row stable transform parallel channels lookup table
entries.body: Stable row softmax requires row maximum subtraction, exponentiation, row sum, and division over the same logical row. Never split a row across independent tiles without combining both maximum and sum. The official MLIR-AIE softmax uses a fixed per-tile kernel and transform_parallel across independent tiles/channels. Use a whole row as the initial tile for the classic corpus. Lookup-table exponential approximations are legal only when the manifest tolerance is met; otherwise emit unsupported operations instead of silently changing accuracy.

entries.title: XDNA2 convolution layout boundaries
entries.tags: conv2d convolution nchw padding kernel vector mac channel layout float32 int8
entries.body: The official optimized IRON convolution examples are shape-, layout-, and dtype-specific. Their vectorized 1x1 int8 kernels use channels-last blocked layouts and cannot be substituted for an FP32 NCHW 3x3 convolution. A correct root should explicitly tile the padded spatial domain and preserve NCHW indexing in a scalar Peano kernel. Only propose channel blocking or vector MAC after the data reordering, halo/padding behavior, kernel ABI, and output layout are all explicit.

entries.title: Intel NPU OpenVINO model construction contract
entries.tags: openvino model opset13 parameter friendly name output static shape build_model
entries.body: model.py must import OpenVINO, define build_model(manifest=None), and return an ov.Model without compiling or running at import time. Create one opset13 Parameter per input tensor with the manifest's static shape and dtype. Explicitly set Parameter and output tensor names with output(0).get_tensor().set_names({manifest_name}); friendly names alone are insufficient. Construct outputs from OpenVINO graph operations, give output tensors their manifest names, and pass the Parameters to ov.Model in deterministic manifest order. Scalars with fixed manifest values should be Constants. Never implement the result with NumPy or a constant precomputed output.

entries.title: Intel NPU graph recipes for the classic operations
entries.tags: add reduce_sum matmul transpose softmax layer_norm attention convolution moving_average power gamma opset13
entries.body: Map semantic operations directly to opset13 graph nodes: Add for elementwise addition; ReduceSum with an int64 axes Constant; MatMul with explicit transpose flags; Transpose with an int64 permutation; Softmax with the declared axis; MVN or ReduceMean/Subtract/Power/Add/Sqrt/Divide/Multiply/Add for layer normalization; MatMul/Transpose/Multiply/Softmax/MatMul for noncausal attention; Convolution for NCHW convolution; and Power after Clamp for gamma correction. Moving average can be represented with Pad plus a fixed one-dimensional convolution only when prefix-window semantics are preserved; otherwise use explicit Slice/Reduce/Concat graph construction. Keep accumulation and output conversions explicit.

entries.title: Intel NPU 4000 offline compilation and blob export
entries.tags: npu compiler plugin platform 4000 offline compile blob export BytesIO
entries.body: For offline Lunar Lake NPU 4000 compilation, call core.compile_model(model, 'NPU', {'NPU_COMPILER_TYPE': 'PLUGIN', 'NPU_PLATFORM': '4000'}). Export the compiled model and validate that the resulting blob is nonempty. Python releases may return a BytesIO-like object; call getvalue when present before writing bytes. Offline compilation proves compiler acceptance, not device correctness or latency. Keep 3720, 5010, and 5020 as different target profiles rather than changing the 4000 property opportunistically.

entries.title: Intel NPU compiler optimization and runtime properties
entries.tags: optimization-level performance hint latency throughput profiling tiles supported properties
entries.body: The NPU plugin advertises supported properties dynamically, so query supported_properties before relying on a device-only option. Compiler optimization-level 0 prioritizes compile time, 1 is balanced, and 2 prioritizes execution performance. performance-hint-override=latency applies only with LATENCY mode. Tile overrides must not exceed the device's reported max_tiles and can reduce cross-device compatibility. Profiling, turbo, throughput, and latency hints affect real execution and must not be used to fabricate offline performance evidence.

entries.title: Intel CPU equivalence and output diagnostics
entries.tags: cpu equivalence oracle input output name dtype shape tolerance mismatch latency diagnostic
entries.body: Compile the generated ov.Model for CPU and feed deterministic manifest inputs by exact Parameter name. Compare every output's count, name/order, shape, dtype, and values with the NumPy oracle using the manifest tolerance before NPU blob compilation is accepted. A mismatch is a semantic failure, not a compiler lesson unless the root cause is demonstrated to be backend-specific. CPU p50/p95 is a host graph diagnostic only and must never be labeled Intel NPU performance.

entries.title: Intel NPU public programming boundary
entries.tags: unsupported public sdk low level kernel openvino graph proprietary format
entries.body: The supported public interface in this framework is an OpenVINO model compiled by the Intel NPU plugin into its proprietary executable format. Do not claim or synthesize an arbitrary low-level ActShave or firmware kernel SDK equivalent to AMD Peano/IRON. When semantics cannot be expressed with supported OpenVINO graph operations, return unsupported_operations instead of embedding host Python execution or silently approximating the kernel.
